set.st: Two stories: (1) 1850, two Germans' land-payment gold vanished from a schooner and was said buried on the stony beach (one 1940 AP feature; legend only); (2) a 1905 wire story that $150,000 in Chicago-fire Spanish gold was dug up here was a hoax invented by a Northport joker. The 1905 wire said two Northport men had dug up the gold after strangers with a robber's chart crossed to the island in a hired launch; the next day both men denied finding any money and said the strangers were looking after timber, and a local paper traced the tale to the village wag. The same report noted that one of the two had been talking to old residents who knew the treasure story, so the legend predates 1905. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself. The 1940 feature gives the last known search as about 1925.
